title: Design exercise: SAA-1.2-S03
scenario: Bramblecote Ticketing sells stadium tickets and sees traffic jump from 300 to 60,000 requests per second within minutes of an on-sale. A penetration test found SQL fragments accepted in query strings, and last month a volumetric network-layer flood (SYN and UDP reflection packets, not HTTP requests) exhausted the site during an on-sale. Its 25 support engineers share IAM user access keys to reach the production account, and the order database password is committed in the application's configuration repository. The auditor wants each of these four weaknesses closed by a control aimed at that weakness, and the CFO wants no appliances and no self-run proxy fleets.
constraints: Do not claim live AWS experience
The CFO rules out appliances and self-managed proxy fleets
The auditor requires each of the four findings to be closed by a distinct control
The database password must be changeable without redeploying the application

rubric.label: Each of the four findings has its own control and no control is claimed to cover two of them
All 25 support engineers reach the account with per-person, temporary access and no shared keys remain

constraint_reason: Mapped as design_exercise to complete skill coverage when no dedicated live lab step exists
